title: File Reading & Pointer Movement: readline() vs Iteration
description: Visualizing file cursor progression, reading line-by-line, stripping newline escapes, and splitting CSV records in memory.

steps.explanation: open('students.txt', 'r') opens the file in read mode. The file pointer is positioned at byte 0 (very start of the file).
file.readline() reads until '\n'. It loads 'Arun,85\n' into variable line1 and moves the file pointer forward by 8 bytes.
line1.strip() removes the trailing newline '\n' character, resulting in a clean string 'Arun,85'.
clean_line1.split(',') splits the string into two tokens: name = 'Arun' and mark = '85'.
Calling file.readline() a second time begins at byte 8 (the saved pointer position). It reads 'Priya,92\n' and advances the pointer.
clean_line2 removes the newline delimiter from the second line, yielding 'Priya,92'.
file.close() closes the file handle and releases system resources. Pointer tracking is finalized.
